definitions.explanation: A third molar tooth, the last teeth to emerge in the back of the mouth, typically appearing in late adolescence or early adulthood. Often associated with dental problems requiring extraction.

examples.japanese: {親知|おやし}らずが{生|は}えてきた。
examples.english: My wisdom tooth is coming in.

examples.japanese: {親知|おやし}らずを{抜|ぬ}いてもらった。
examples.english: I had my wisdom tooth pulled.

examples.japanese: {下|した}の{親知|おやし}らずが{横向|よこむ}きに{生|は}えていて、{痛|いた}みがある。
examples.english: My lower wisdom tooth is growing in sideways and it hurts.

examples.japanese: {歯医者|はいしゃ}に{親知|おやし}らずの{抜歯|ばっし}を{勧|すす}められたが、{怖|こわ}くてまだ{決|き}められない。
examples.english: The dentist recommended extracting my wisdom tooth, but I'm scared and can't decide yet.

notes:
Literally "{親|おや}が{知|し}らない{歯|は}" — "the tooth the parent doesn't know about," because wisdom teeth emerge after a child has grown up and left parental oversight. This folk etymology gives the word a distinctly Japanese flavor compared to the English "wisdom tooth" (which emphasizes the age of wisdom).

Wisdom tooth extraction ({親知|おやし}らずの{抜歯|ばっし}) is a common topic of conversation in Japan, as with many cultures. The teeth frequently cause problems by growing in at an angle ({横向|よこむ}きに{生|は}える) or becoming impacted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {親知|おやし}らずを{抜|ぬ}く: to extract a wisdom tooth
- {親知|おやし}らずが{生|は}える: a wisdom tooth comes in
- {親知|おやし}らずが{痛|いた}い: one's wisdom tooth hurts
- {親知|おやし}らずの{抜歯|ばっし}: wisdom tooth extraction
- {上|うえ}の{親知|おやし}らず / {下|した}の{親知|おやし}らず: upper / lower wisdom tooth

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奥歯|おくば}: back tooth, molar — a broader term for any molar, not just wisdom teeth
- {乳歯|にゅうし}: baby tooth, milk tooth — the teeth that fall out in childhood, a different stage of dental development
- {永久歯|えいきゅうし}: permanent tooth — the adult teeth that replace baby teeth
